title: Round the Ring
statement: Five numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ and $e$ satisfy the following: the average of $a$ and $b$ is $8$, the average of $b$ and $c$ is $15$, the average of $c$ and $d$ is $17$, the average of $d$ and $e$ is $13$, and the average of $e$ and $a$ is $10$. What is the value of $a$?
hints: Rewrite each average as a sum of two of the numbers. How many of these five sums does each number appear in?
Add all five pair sums. Each of $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$, $e$ appears in exactly two of them, so the result is $2(a+b+c+d+e)$.
The pair sums are $16, 30, 34, 26, 20$, which add up to $126$, so $a+b+c+d+e=63$. The two sums $b+c$ and $d+e$ together contain every number except $a$.
solution:
The conditions say $a+b=16$, $b+c=30$, $c+d=34$, $d+e=26$ and $e+a=20$. Each number appears in exactly two of these sums. Adding all five gives $2(a+b+c+d+e)=126$, so $a+b+c+d+e=63$. Then $a=63-(b+c)-(d+e)=63-30-26=7$.

The answer is $7$.
